name: UPPAbaby Cruz V3
price_note: Stroller only; bassinet and Mesa/Aria car seat sold separately. BabyGearLab list $900.
recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for the Cruz (CPSC title search; recall CSV). UPPAbaby's 2016–2026 recalls cover RumbleSeat adapters (21-158) and the RIDGE jogger (22-215), not the Cruz.
why: Two independent testers agree: BabyGearLab ranks it #1 of 20 full-size strollers (79, Best Full-Size Stroller for Most, Aug 2026) and Wirecutter names it its top pick (Mar 2026). No recall, a single-action colour-coded brake, and a lay-flat seat UPPAbaby rates from birth.
cautions: Not for jogging
Pricey; bassinet is extra
Cannot convert to a double (choose the Vista V3 for that)

name: UPPAbaby Vista V3
price_note: Most colours $999.99 on uppababy.com (one colour $899.99). BabyGearLab lists $1,200; RumbleSeat for double mode is extra.

specs.child_range: Birth with bassinet/SnugSeat, otherwise 3 months–50 lb, up to 40 in

recall_status: No recall of the Vista V3 itself. CPSC 21-158 (Jun 2021): adapters included with UPPAbaby RumbleSeats (the Vista double-mode seat) could detach, about 86,000 units; check older adapters.
why: Ties the Cruz V3 at 79 on BabyGearLab (#2 of 20, High-Quality for Bigger Families) and is Wirecutter's upgrade pick for double strollers; ranked just below the Cruz because of the past RumbleSeat-adapter recall and its larger, heavier frame.
cautions: Large fold; heavy (27.9 lb measured)
Seat alone from 3 months; use bassinet or car seat for newborns
Register RumbleSeat adapters (21-158 recall history)

name: Nuna SWIV
price_note: Base colours $1,000 (some $1,050); includes travel-system adapter. Bassinet sold separately.

specs.child_range: Up to 50 lb (newborn via PIPA car seat or bassinet)

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 (CPSC title search for Nuna returns only 2016 high chairs; recall CSV).
why: Consumer Reports' 2026 Top Pick for travel systems is the SWIV + PIPA aire rx, with 'near-perfect ratings' for the stroller in CR's ease-of-use, safety and maneuverability tests; no recall. Ranked below the UPPAbabys because only one lab has tested it and CR's numbers are paywalled.
cautions: CR says it 'feels a little heavy and large'
Evidence comes from CR's travel-system test; no BabyGearLab or Wirecutter result
Bassinet extra for newborn lie-flat use
sources: Consumer Reports top picks for travel systems (May 2026)

name: Baby Jogger City Mini GT2
price_note: BabyGearLab list price. babyjogger.com showed the GT2 out of stock on Sep 3, 2026 (archived page); successor City Mini GT3 is on sale but has not been tested by BabyGearLab or Wirecutter.
recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for Baby Jogger strollers (last stroller recalls 2009–2012).
why: Wirecutter's pick for off-roading among full-size strollers and its top side-by-side double (GT2 Double); BabyGearLab scores it 59 (#8 of 20). Clean recall record and a 65 lb limit, but BabyGearLab calls it below average overall.
cautions: Being replaced by the GT3; GT2 out of stock on babyjogger.com
Hand-operated parking brake 'takes some finessing' (BabyGearLab)
Newborn use via car seat adapter; no included bassinet

name: Nuna MIXX next
price_note: Stroller only; bassinet sold separately. BabyGearLab list $900.
recall_status: None found 2016–2026 (CPSC title search for Nuna; recall CSV).
why: Tested by two labs: BabyGearLab 62 (#6 of 20) and a Wirecutter 'worth considering' mention for the easiest fold. Both flagged stability: Wirecutter said big bumps 'threatened to tip it over' with 36 lb aboard, and BabyGearLab notes a 'possible tip-over risk' from the short wheelbase off-road.
cautions: Tip-over concern on bumps/rough ground (Wirecutter, BabyGearLab)
Brake-adjacent pocket gets kicked when setting the brake
Small 11 lb basket per BabyGearLab

name: Baby Jogger City Select 2
price_note: Standard City Select 2 on babyjogger.com (archived Sep 6, 2026); Eco Collection $749.99. Second seat extra.

specs.child_range: Seat from 6 months, up to 45 lb / 40 in (BabyGearLab)

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for Baby Jogger strollers.
why: Single-to-double with a lab score: BabyGearLab 56 (#13 of 20), 'not a good single stroller' because of weight, but single-action brakes and no recall. Wirecutter found the fold on the closely related City Select Lux sometimes stuck.
cautions: Heavy (27.2 lb measured, one seat)
Wirecutter: City Select Lux fold 'seemed to stick' (same fold mechanism)
Seat from 6 months; newborns need car seat or bassinet

name: Britax Brook+
price_note: Stroller only on us.britax.com; BabyGearLab list $330.

specs.child_range: Up to 50 lb / 44 in; newborn via Britax infant car seat

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for the Brook/Brook+. Britax stroller recalls in the window are B-Ready (16-080) and B-Agile/BOB Click & Go (17-088), different models.
why: BabyGearLab scores it 56 (#12 of 20) and calls it basic but light and cheap; ranked below the City Select 2 because BabyGearLab warns its double-action brakes are easy to half-set.
cautions: Double-action (two-pedal) parking brake
Hard to push and turn in BabyGearLab tests
Bulky fold for its size

name: Chicco Corso Primo Modular Stroller
price_note: Corso Primo stroller only on chiccousa.com (Summit colour).

specs.child_range: Up to 50 lb; newborn via infant insert or Chicco car seat

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for Chicco strollers (only Chicco recall in the window is the MyFit booster, 25C-005).
why: Consumer Reports has tested the Corso Primo, but its score is paywalled; no BabyGearLab or Wirecutter result. Clean recall record and native click-in for every Chicco infant seat (KeyFit family) put it above strollers with weaker records.
cautions: CR rating not visible; no published independent score
Heavier than it looks (26 lb with toddler seat)

name: Mockingbird Single-to-Double 3.0
price_note: Frame + one seat; 2nd Seat Kit $175, bassinet and car-seat adapter extra. Some colours sold out on Oct 4, 2026.

specs.child_range: 3 months–50 lb (45 lb per seat as a double); from birth with insert, bassinet or car-seat adapter

recall_status: Earlier versions recalled: CPSC 23-042 (Nov 2022, ~149,000 Single-to-Double, frame cracks, 138 reports, 8 injuries) and 23-161 (Mar 2023, Single). No recall found for the 3.0.
why: Consumer Reports has tested the sibling Mockingbird 3.0 Single (score paywalled; the Single-to-Double itself is untested) and Mockingbird says it meets ASTM F833-21, but the brand's 2022–23 frame-crack recalls of about 174,000 strollers and Wirecutter finding earlier versions 'a little precarious' keep it near the bottom.
cautions: Prior frame-crack recalls (check lot numbers on used units)
The Bump tester reported a near-tip in tandem mode (anecdote)
Wide 26 in frame; 36 lb with two seats

name: Graco Modes Nest Stroller
price_note: Stroller only on gracobaby.com (archived Sep 3, 2026); travel system with SnugRide DLX $479.99.

specs.child_range: Up to 50 lb; from birth with a Graco infant car seat

recall_status: Stroller not recalled. NHTSA 26C-003 (Apr 2026) covers the Modes Nest Travel System bundled with the SnugRide Turn & Slide seat (model 7DP08NRI, made Dec 2025–Mar 2026): carrier may detach from base in a crash.
why: Lowest-scoring candidate with a lab result: BabyGearLab 52 (#17 of 20, 'meh'), with double-action brakes it warns are easy to half-set, and a 2026 recall of one travel-system bundle's car seat.
cautions: Double-action (two-pedal) parking brake
Poor canopy coverage; bulky fold
If bought as Turn & Slide bundle, check 26C-003
